data.name: Chandak
data.gender_notes: Chandak is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Chandra' meaning 'Moon'. This name is dedicated to Lord Chandrama, the Moon God in Hindu mythology, representing calmness, wisdom, and protection. The name Chandak carries the meaning “Moon God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chandak usually hope their child will grow to embody moon god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by the Moon God, symbolizing divine guidance and protection.
data.etymology: Chandak belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chandak total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Chandak" is deeply rooted in Hindu culture and is popular among communities in India and the South Asian region. Naming children after celestial bodies, especially the Moon, is a common practice in Indian culture, reflecting reverence for the divine and the natural world. The name represents a connection to ancient traditions and symbols, and it is believed to bestow blessings and good fortune upon the child.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Chandak" contains spiritual significance, as it is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Chandra', meaning the 'Moon'. In Hindu mythology, the Moon God, also known as Chandrama, is revered as the ruler of the night and the provider of light during the dark hours. He embodies attributes of calmness, serenity, and tranquility. By giving a child this name, parents commonlty hope that he or she will embody these qualities, growing up to be wise, balanced, and peaceful individuals. Additionally, the name is a reminder of the divine presence and influence in the world and in one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chandak: Moon's Radiance. A name that reflects the inner luminosity and emotional depth, symbolizing the connection to the subconscious self and the powerful influence of the lunar cycle on one's emotions and intuition.

historical_references.reference: Chandaka was a king of the Vanga kingdom in ancient India. He ruled during the 2nd century BCE and is believed to have extended the territorial boundaries of the Vangas.

Chandaka is also mentioned in Buddhist literature as a wealthy merchant who donated a grove of trees to the Buddhist monk Anathapindika. This event is believed to have taken place during the 3rd century BCE.
